title: Best Women's Golf Shirts UK
short: Ten women's golf polo shirts tested on the course by Golf Monthly's female contributors, compared on fit, fabric and feel.
intro: A good golf shirt needs to move with your swing, wick sweat and still look good off the course. This guide is based on Golf Monthly's tested roundup (updated May 2026), led by women's editor Alison Root with a team of female contributors who wore each shirt while playing golf. Golf Monthly tests around 20 shirts each year; these are 10 of them. Prices vary by retailer, so no prices are shown; use the search link on each pick.

products.name: ArmourDry Women's Short Sleeve Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who sweat a lot and want a fitted shirt that doesn't cling
products.key_spec: 80% cotton, 20% polyester, UA Helix Technology, XS-2XL, 5 colours
products.summary: The tester found it very comfortable and airy despite being fairly fitted, thanks to UA Helix Technology that wicks sweat, speeds up drying and encourages airflow, giving great odour control. The body felt slightly short after finishing a golf swing, though it's long enough to tuck into a mid to high waisted skort, with pretty pearlised button detailing.
pros: Controls sweat and odour all round
cons: Felt slightly short in the body
products.search: Under Armour ArmourDry Women's Short Sleeve Polo golf

products.name: Botanical Jacquard Floral Polo
products.best_for: Cool-weather rounds where you want a sweater-like feel with golf performance
products.key_spec: 55% cotton, 45% viscose, ribbed collar and hem, longer sleeves, XS-2XL
products.summary: The tester found this cotton mix polo feels more like a sweater than a polo shirt, with a stunning botanical navy print and thick ribbed hem, and longer sleeves that suit a cooler day. The fit is loose yet flattering and the fabric doesn't cling, with five pearlescent buttons each featuring a gold-edged 'Pete the Penguin' logo. It's better suited to cooler days than hot ones due to the thicker material.
pros: High quality feel and finishing touches
A great option for cooler days
cons: More suited to cooler days due to thick material
products.search: Original Penguin Botanical Jacquard Floral Polo golf

products.name: Short Sleeve Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want a standout print in an incredibly light, airy fabric
products.summary: The tester loved the 'Clouds' print of blues and white and found the fabric incredibly light and airy, staying comfortable while playing. It runs true to size but feels roomy with no restrictions, and is the perfect length to wear tucked or untucked, with neat stitching around the sleeve cuffs adding a luxurious look.
cons: Pass if you prefer solid colours

products.name: Maritime Valley Short Sleeve Jersey Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want a classic, collared look that performs like a gym top
products.summary: The tester found brilliant technology behind a traditional-looking polo: breathable and lightweight enough to perform like a gym top, while looking like a classy collared shirt. It's more generous in length than many golf shirts, wicks moisture and dries fast, and can be worn tucked or untucked. Only available in one colour.
products.search: Peter Millar Maritime Valley Short Sleeve Jersey Polo golf

products.name: Core Performance Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want a bold, joyful print with UPF 50 sun protection
products.key_spec: 88% polyester, 12% spandex, UPF 50, anti-odour, XS-XL, 15-20 rotating prints
products.summary: The tester couldn't help but smile pulling this out of the drawer thanks to its bold, joyful print, with fabric that's incredibly soft and lightweight against the skin, plus UPF 50 sun protection and anti-odour protection to stay fresh after 18 holes. The relaxed fit doesn't feel clingy, and side splits at the hem suit wearing it untucked, finished with an embroidered 'Birdie' on the placket.

specs.Colours: 15-20 active prints and colourways at any time

pros: Extremely soft fabric with UPF 50 protection
products.search: Bad Birdie Core Performance Polo golf

products.name: Miley Polo Shirt
products.best_for: Golfers who want a sporty, breathable shirt with sun protection at the neck
products.key_spec: 88% polyester, 12% elastane, stand-up zip collar, XS-2XL
products.summary: The tester found a shirt that feels every bit the sporty top, offering breathability, amazing stretch and comfort, reminiscent of a cycling top without as much cling. The neck zips up to a stand-up collar offering sun protection at the back. It feels cool to touch, so a midlayer may be needed when the sun goes in, and the colour palette is fairly muted.
pros: Breathable, quick-drying material keeps you cool
Stand-up collar adds a sporty touch
products.search: Galvin Green Miley Polo Shirt golf

products.name: Classic Cable Polo Shirt
products.best_for: Golfers who want a shirt that looks equally at home off the course
products.key_spec: 100% cotton, slim all-over cable knit, XXS-XXXL, 1 colour
products.summary: The tester said it looks like something you'd grab off the rail in a high street store rather than the golf course, classically stylish with a slim, all-over cable knit. It felt incredibly soft and comfortable when swinging, though the tester would avoid it on scorching days since the fabric is weightier than standard polyester. The ribbed hem kept its shape well over 18 holes.
pros: Comfortable and holds its shape after 18 holes
cons: Form-fitting cut may not suit every preference
products.search: Rohnisch Classic Cable Polo Shirt golf

products.name: Maisie Golf Shirt
products.best_for: Golfers who want an eye-catching, high-quality shirt with a choice of prints
products.key_spec: 88% polyester, 12% elastane, printed side panels and stand-up collar, XS-XXL, 4 prints
products.summary: The tester found high-quality fabric with a silky-soft finish and plenty of stretch, with printed panels at the side and on the collar, cuffs and zip making it eye-catching. Side slits add to the feminine shape, and the streamlined side panels give the impression of a dress when paired with a matching skort, with four prints to choose from.
cons: Not for those who dislike prints

products.name: Cloudspun Wavey Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want a roomy, silky-feeling shirt with moisture-wicking
products.key_spec: 94% polyester, 6% elastane, regular fit, four-button placket, XS-XXL, 3 colours
products.summary: The tester loved the silky-velvety, lightweight fabric, which looks like animal print at first glance but isn't. It's a regular, roomy fit with plenty of freedom when swinging, and moisture-wicking properties kept the tester cool and comfortable on a warm day. It looks equally good tucked or untucked, with side slits at the hem.

products.name: Katie Top
products.best_for: Golfers who want a lightweight, luxurious-feeling top with a distinctive collar
products.key_spec: 100% polyester, baseball collar with open V-neck, side-slit hem, XS-XL, 3 colours
products.summary: The tester loved the lightweight, stretchy fabric with an almost silky sheen for a luxurious look, and the baseball collar with an open V-neck bound in a lighter colour makes it unique. Side panel detailing creates a flattering shape, and the side-slit hem and ideal length made it comfortable worn loosely on the outside. The tester notes it sizes up, so consider going a size larger.
cons: Fairly fitted shape might not suit everyone

guide.q: What fabric should I look for?
guide.a: Polyester and spandex blends, like the Puma Cloudspun and Bad Birdie, are lightweight and stretchy for swinging freely and dry fast. Cotton blends like the Original Penguin and Rohnisch feel softer and more like everyday wear but suit cooler days better than hot ones, as testers found them warmer.

guide.q: Which shirt suits hot weather best?
guide.a: Golf Monthly's testers found the Famara ('incredibly light and airy'), Peter Millar (performs 'like a gym top') and Puma Cloudspun kept them cool and comfortable in warm conditions, while the Original Penguin and Rohnisch are better suited to cooler days.

guide.q: Does length matter when tucking in?
guide.a: Yes. Testers noted the Under Armour felt slightly short after a golf swing, while the Peter Millar and Dunning shirts were praised for being generous or exactly the right length to stay tucked in throughout a round.

If you want to stand out, the Bad Birdie, Famara and Glenmuir all offer striking prints that testers loved, though Golf Monthly notes these suit the 'pattern-confident'. For a more classic look, the Peter Millar or Rohnisch offer understated, timeless styling.
